q-38601.name: Question 1
q-38601.problem:
By changing the order of integration in the following double integrals, express the following sum as a single double integral.

$$
{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{x}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{2}^{4}{\int }_{0}^{4-x}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$
q-38601.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14163455/assets/ea36f1ec1ddeb03dd8d133fb8d65b5d50b3fa07ba34495978d87f95742dee042.png)

The diagram above shows the region of integration. It consists of two type I regions, given by

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le x\}\,\cup \,\{(x,y)\,:\,2\le x\le 4,\,0\le y\le 4-x\}.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the left boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x),$ is

$$
y=x\,⟹\,x=y
$$

and the right boundary of the region is

$$
y=4-x\,⟹\,x=4-y.
$$

To change the order of integration we write $D$ as a type II region. The type II representation of the region is

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 2,\,y\le x\le 4-y\},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14163455/assets/e82098a4bb63f1d709a06b6a24da078594716d6a3cc0fa2e069af9dcd9154955.png)

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{x}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{2}^{4}{\int }_{0}^{4-x}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{y}^{4-y}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1
?

By changing the order of integration in the following double integrals, express the following sum as a single double integral.

∫02∫0xf(x,y)dydx+∫24∫04−xf(x,y)dydx

a
∫02∫y4−yf(x,y)dxdy
b
∫04∫4−yyf(x,y)dxdy
c
∫04∫y4−yf(x,y)dxdy
d
∫y4−y∫04f(x,y)dxdy
e
∫02∫4−yyf(x,y)dxdy
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The diagram above shows the region of integration. It consists of two type I regions, given by

D={(x,y):0≤x≤2,0≤y≤x}∪{(x,y):2≤x≤4,0≤y≤4−x}.

Notice that the left boundary of the region, written in the form y=y(x), is

y=x⟹x=y

and the right boundary of the region is

y=4−x⟹x=4−y.

To change the order of integration we write D as a type II region. The type II representation of the region is

D={(x,y):0≤y≤2,y≤x≤4−y},

as shown in the diagram below.

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain

∫02∫0xf(x,y)dydx+∫24∫04−xf(x,y)dydx=∫02∫y4−yf(x,y)dxdy.

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,x\le y\le 1\}.
$$

Notice that the left boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x)$ is

$$
x=0,
$$

and the right boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x),$ is

$$
y=x\,⟹\,x=y.
$$

To change the order of integration, we write $D$ as type II region. Its type II representation is

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,0\le x\le y\},

q-82253.problem:
By changing the order of integration in the following double integrals, express the following sum as a single double integral.

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2{x}^{2}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{4-2x}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$
q-82253.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14163455/assets/8359a189981b238d0851324a896ed0a3a9aa0620e8cf4d38228752ff484b4cd0.png)

The diagram above shows the region of integration. It consists of two type I regions, given by

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 2{x}^{2}\}\,\cup \,\{(x,y)\,:\,1\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le 2(x-2)^{2}\}.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the left boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x),$ is

$$
y=2{x}^{2}\,⟹\,x=\sqrt{\frac{y}{2}}
$$

and the right boundary of the region is

$$
y=4-2x\,⟹\,x=\frac{4-y}{2}.
$$

To change the order of integration we write $D$ as a type II region. The type II representation of the region is

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 2,\,\sqrt{\frac{y}{2}}\le x\le \frac{4-y}{2}\},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14163455/assets/bee5de8ca9011672a159686d1547a909e5288097b15241f5004e5c788459ee70.png)

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2{x}^{2}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2(x-2)^{2}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{\sqrt{y/2}}^{(4-y)/2}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3

By changing the order of integration in the following double integrals, express the following sum as a single double integral.

∫01∫02x2f(x,y)dydx+∫12∫04−2xf(x,y)dydx

a
∫y/22∫0(4−y)/2f(x,y)dxdy
b
∫02∫y/2(4−y)/2f(x,y)dxdy
c
∫y/2(4−y)/2∫02f(x,y)dxdy
d
∫0(4−y)/2∫y/22f(x,y)dxdy
e
∫0y/2∫(4−y)/22f(x,y)dxdy
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The diagram above shows the region of integration. It consists of two type I regions, given by

D={(x,y):0≤x≤1,0≤y≤2x2}∪{(x,y):1≤x≤2,0≤y≤2(x−2)2}.

Notice that the left boundary of the region, written in the form y=y(x), is

y=2x2⟹x=y2

and the right boundary of the region is

y=4−2x⟹x=4−y2.

To change the order of integration we write D as a type II region. The type II representation of the region is

D={(x,y):0≤y≤2,y2≤x≤4−y2},

as shown in the diagram below.

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain

∫01∫02x2f(x,y)dydx+∫12∫02(x−2)2f(x,y)dydx=∫02∫y/2(4−y)/2f(x,y)dxdy.

q-132565.problem:
By changing the order of integration in the following double integrals, express the following sum as a single double integral.

$$
{\int }_{1-e}^{0}{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-y)}^{1}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{0}^{e-1}{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡(y+1)}^{1}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y
$$
q-132565.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14163455/assets/3426e7bdd134bc9af5a3665f8c9c55a65514afa9dca5be112eabb37479c4c9ec.png)

The diagram above shows the region of integration. It consists of two type II regions, given by

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =\{(x,y)\,:\,1-e\le y\le 0,\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-y)\le x\le 1\}\,\cup \,\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le e-1,\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(y+1)\le x\le 1\}.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the top boundary of the region, written in the form $x=x(y),$ is

$$
x=\operatorname{ln}⁡(y+1)\,⟹\,y={e}^{x}-1,
$$

and the bottom boundary of the region is

$$
x=\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-y)\,⟹\,y=1-{e}^{x}.
$$

To change the order of integration, we write $D$ as a type I region. The type I representation of the region is

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,1-{e}^{x}\le y\le {e}^{x}-1\},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14163455/assets/7d88d351b481859ec3e77350d3679387836d2e7f67325caca50e2f61cce9dcce.png)

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1-e}^{0}{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-y)}^{1}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{0}^{e-1}{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡(y+1)}^{1}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1-{e}^{x}}^{{e}^{x}-1}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4
?

By changing the order of integration in the following double integrals, express the following sum as a single double integral. ∫1−e0∫ln⁡(1−y)1f(x,y)dxdy+∫0e−1∫ln⁡(y+1)1f(x,y)dxdy

a
∫−11∫−1−exex+1f(x,y)dydx
b
∫−11∫1−exex−1f(x,y)dydx
c
∫01∫1−exex−1f(x,y)dydx
d
∫01∫−1−exex+1f(x,y)dydx
e
∫−10∫1−exex−1f(x,y)dydx
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The diagram above shows the region of integration. It consists of two type II regions, given by D={(x,y):1−e≤y≤0,ln⁡(1−y)≤x≤1}∪{(x,y):0≤y≤e−1,ln⁡(y+1)≤x≤1}.

Notice that the top boundary of the region, written in the form x=x(y), is x=ln⁡(y+1)⟹y=ex−1, and the bottom boundary of the region is x=ln⁡(1−y)⟹y=1−ex.

To change the order of integration, we write D as a type I region. The type I representation of the region is D={(x,y):0≤x≤1,1−ex≤y≤ex−1}, as shown in the diagram below.

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain ∫1−e0∫ln⁡(1−y)1f(x,y)dxdy+∫0e−1∫ln⁡(y+1)1f(x,y)dxdy=∫01∫1−exex−1f(x,y)dydx.

The diagram above shows the region of integration. It is a type II region, and its type II representation is

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,-4\le y\le -1,\,1\le x\le -\frac{4}{y}\}.
$$

Notice that the top boundary of the region, written in the form $x=x(y),$ is

$$
y=-1,
$$

and the bottom boundary of the region is

$$
x=-\frac{4}{y}\,⟹\,y=-\frac{4}{x},
$$

To change the order of integration, we write $D$ as a type I region. The type I representation of the region is

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,1\le x\le 4,\,-\frac{4}{x}\le y\le -1\},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14163455/assets/3338ee0f8bdc6f18bb5a56b12a36d31d79c87db6c39686adc7ae7c00efb9d526.png)

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-4}^{-1}{\int }_{1}^{-4/y}\frac{1}{\sqrt{4\operatorname{ln}⁡x-x+2}}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y & ={\int }_{1}^{4}{\int }_{-4/x}^{-1}\frac{1}{\sqrt{4\operatorname{ln}⁡x-x+2}}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{4}\frac{1}{\sqrt{4\operatorname{ln}⁡x-x+2}}[{\int }_{-4/x}^{-1}\text{d}y]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{4}\frac{1}{\sqrt{4\operatorname{ln}⁡x-x+2}}\cdot y\,{|}_{-4/x}^{-1}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{4}(\frac{4}{x}-1)\frac{1}{\sqrt{4\operatorname{ln}⁡x-x+2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\sqrt{4\operatorname{ln}⁡x-x+2}\,{|}_{1}^{4} \\  & =2\sqrt{4\operatorname{ln}⁡4-4+2}-2\sqrt{4\operatorname{ln}⁡1-1+2} \\  & =2\sqrt{4\operatorname{ln}⁡4-2}-2 \\  & =2(\sqrt{8\operatorname{ln}⁡2-2}-1)\end{aligned}
$$
